projects.title: Dijkstra's Shortest Path Algorithm with Priority Queue (Min-Heap)
projects.description: Dijkstra's algorithm computes the shortest path distances from a single source vertex to all other vertices in a weighted graph with NON-NEGATIVE edge weights. Using a Priority Queue (Min-Heap) reduces time complexity from naive `O(V^2)` down to optimal `O((V + E) log V)`! In this project, you will build Dijkstra Shortest Path Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Dijkstra's Algorithm Architecture, Min-Heap Priority Queues & Non-Negative Edge Guarantees
projects.exampleText: Compute shortest paths from source vertex 0
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Dijkstra's Shortest Path Algorithm (Min-Heap) ---
Shortest Distances from Source 0: [ 0: 0, 1: 4, 2: 7, 3: 11 ]
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Distances Array**: Initialize `dist[source] = 0`, all other `dist[i] = INF`.
2. **Min-Heap Extraction**: Extract minimum distance node `u`; relax unvisited neighbors `v`: if `dist[u] + weight < dist[v]`, update `dist[v]` and push to Min-Heap.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `dijkstra_demo()`: Solves single-source shortest path using Dijkstra's algorithm.

projects.title: Prim's Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) Algorithm
projects.description: Prim's algorithm finds a Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) for a connected weighted undirected graph by growing the tree one vertex at a time starting from an arbitrary root node. Uses a Min-Heap Priority Queue to greedily select the minimum weight edge connecting an unvisited vertex in `O(E log V)` time! In this project, you will build Prim's MST Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Prim's MST Greedy Selection, Cut Property Principles & Min-Heap Edge Extractions
projects.exampleText: Compute total Minimum Spanning Tree weight via Prim's algorithm
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Prim's Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) Algorithm ---
Minimum Spanning Tree Weight (Prim's) = 16
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Cut Property**: Greedily extract lowest weight edge extending from current tree to non-tree vertex.
2. **Priority Queue**: Update candidate edge weights for unvisited adjacent vertices.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `prim_mst_demo()`: Solves Minimum Spanning Tree using Prim's algorithm.

projects.title: Kruskal's Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) Algorithm using DSU
projects.description: Kruskal's algorithm computes an MST by sorting ALL graph edges by weight in ascending order, then greedily adding edges one by one using Disjoint Set Union (DSU) to prevent cycle formation in `O(E log E)` time! In this project, you will build Kruskal's MST Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Kruskal's Edge Sorting, DSU Cycle Avoidance & Greedy MST Construction
projects.exampleText: Compute total Minimum Spanning Tree weight via Kruskal's algorithm
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Kruskal's Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) Algorithm ---
Minimum Spanning Tree Weight (Kruskal's DSU) = 16
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Edge Sort**: Sort edges array by weight ascending.
2. **DSU Union**: Add edge `(u, v)` to MST if `union_sets(u, v)` succeeds without creating cycle.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `kruskal_mst_demo()`: Solves Minimum Spanning Tree using Kruskal's DSU algorithm.

projects.title: Bellman-Ford Shortest Path Algorithm with Negative Weight Cycle Detection
projects.description: Dijkstra fails on graphs with negative edge weights. The Bellman-Ford algorithm handles NEGATIVE edge weights by relaxing all E edges `V - 1` times in `O(V * E)` time. If an edge can STILL be relaxed on the `V`-th pass, a NEGATIVE WEIGHT CYCLE exists! In this project, you will build Bellman-Ford Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Bellman-Ford Relaxation Sweeps, Negative Edge Handling & Negative Cycle Detection
projects.exampleText: Compute shortest path with negative edge weights and detect negative cycles
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Bellman-Ford Shortest Path Algorithm ---
Shortest Distances: [ 0: 0, 1: 2, 2: 5, 3: 1 ]
Negative Weight Cycle Detected: NO
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **V-1 Edge Relaxations**: For `i = 1 .. V-1`, relax all edges `(u, v, w)`.
2. **V-th Pass Detection**: If `dist[u] + w < dist[v]` on V-th pass, return true for negative cycle.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `bellman_ford_demo()`: Solves single-source shortest path and detects negative cycles via Bellman-Ford.

projects.title: Floyd-Warshall All-Pairs Shortest Path Algorithm
projects.description: The Floyd-Warshall algorithm computes shortest path distances between ALL PAIRS of vertices `(i, j)` in a weighted directed graph in `O(V^3)` time using Dynamic Programming! Formula: `dist[i][j] = min(dist[i][j], dist[i][k] + dist[k][j])`. In this project, you will build Floyd-Warshall Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: All-Pairs Shortest Paths (APSP), Dynamic Programming Matrix Triple Loops & Intermediate Node Relaxation
projects.exampleText: Compute all-pairs shortest path matrix in O(V^3) time
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Floyd-Warshall All-Pairs Shortest Path Algorithm ---
All-Pairs Shortest Path Matrix Computed in O(V^3) time.
Distance (0 → 3) = 8
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Triple Loop**: Outer loop `k` represents intermediate vertex, inner loops `i` and `j` represent source/dest.
2. **DP Recurrence**: `dist[i][j] = min(dist[i][j], dist[i][k] + dist[k][j])`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `floyd_warshall_demo()`: Computes all-pairs shortest path matrix using Floyd-Warshall algorithm.

projects.title: Shortest Path in Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) via Topological Sort
projects.description: In a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG), shortest paths from a source to all vertices can be computed in LINEAR `O(V + E)` time! Sort DAG vertices topologically, then relax outgoing edges of each vertex in topological order. In this project, you will build DAG Linear Shortest Path Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: DAG Linear Shortest Paths, Topological Order Edge Relaxations & Optimal O(V + E) Complexity
projects.exampleText: Compute shortest paths in DAG in O(V + E) time
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Shortest Path in DAG via Topological Sort ---
Computed DAG shortest paths in linear O(V + E) time.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Topological Order**: Sort DAG vertices topologically.
2. **Linear Relaxation**: Relax outgoing edges in topological order sequence.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `dag_shortest_path_demo()`: Solves DAG shortest paths in O(V + E) time.

projects.title: Single-Source Shortest Path Path Reconstruction
projects.description: Distance arrays store shortest path lengths, but users need the EXACT sequence of visited nodes on the path. Maintain a `parent[u]` pointer array updated during edge relaxations: `parent[v] = u`. Reconstruct the path backwards from destination to source in O(V) time! In this project, you will build Shortest Path Reconstructor in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Shortest Path Node Reconstruction, Parent Pointer Tracing & Path Sequence Retrieval
projects.exampleText: Reconstruct path sequence from source to destination
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Single-Source Shortest Path Path Reconstruction ---
Reconstructed Path (0 → 3): [ 0 → 1 → 4 → 3 ]
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Parent Pointer**: Set `parent[v] = u` whenever edge relaxation succeeds.
2. **Backtrack Path**: Follow parent pointers from `destination` to `source`; reverse array.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `path_reconstruction_demo()`: Reconstructs exact node path sequence from shortest path algorithms.

projects.title: Second Minimum Spanning Tree Finder
projects.description: Find the Second Minimum Spanning Tree (2nd Best MST) of a graph. Build primary MST using Kruskal's algorithm. For each edge NOT in primary MST, add it to tree (creating a cycle) and remove the heaviest edge on that cycle in `O(V * E)` time! In this project, you will build 2nd Best MST Finder in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Second Best MST Algorithms, Tree Edge Swapping & Cycle Max Edge Removals
projects.exampleText: Find weight of primary MST and second best MST
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Second Minimum Spanning Tree Finder ---
Primary MST Weight = 16
Second Best MST Weight = 18
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Primary MST**: Compute primary MST edges set `T`.
2. **Edge Swap**: For non-tree edge `e(u, v)`, replace max weight edge on path `u → v` in `T`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `second_mst_demo()`: Finds second minimum spanning tree.

projects.title: Network Delay Time (Dijkstra Signal Propagation)
projects.description: Given N network nodes and directed travel times `times[i] = (u, v, w)`, find minimum time for all N nodes to receive a signal sent from source node K. Run Dijkstra's algorithm: return `max(dist[1..N])` (or -1 if any node unreachable) in `O(E log V)` time! In this project, you will build Network Delay Time Solver in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Signal Propagation Modeling, Max Distance Extractions & Network Delay Evaluation
projects.exampleText: Compute minimum time for all network nodes to receive signal
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Network Delay Time (Dijkstra Signal Propagation) ---
Minimum time for all nodes to receive signal = 9
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Dijkstra Search**: Run Dijkstra starting from source node K.
2. **Max Distance**: Maximum distance among all nodes gives network signal propagation time.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `network_delay_time_demo()`: Solves Network Delay Time using Dijkstra's algorithm.

projects.title: Min Cost to Connect Cities (Prim's vs Kruskal's Benchmark)
projects.description: Compare execution performance of Prim's algorithm vs Kruskal's algorithm on dense vs sparse city connection graphs. Measure execution time microsecond metrics and prove Prim's excels on dense graphs `O(V^2)` while Kruskal's excels on sparse graphs `O(E log V)`. In this project, you will build MST Performance Benchmark Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: MST Algorithm Benchmarking, Dense vs Sparse Graph Performance & Execution Metrics
projects.exampleText: Benchmark Prim's vs Kruskal's execution times on dense city graph
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Min Cost to Connect Cities (Prim's vs Kruskal's Benchmark) ---
Prim's Execution Time: 0.12ms
Kruskal's Execution Time: 0.15ms
Identical Total MST Cost = 350
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Dense Graph**: Prim's `O(V^2)` avoids sorting E edges.
2. **Sparse Graph**: Kruskal's `O(E log V)` runs faster when `E << V^2`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `mst_benchmark_demo()`: Benchmarks Prim's vs Kruskal's MST algorithms.

projects.title: Cheapest Flights Within K Stops (Bellman-Ford / BFS DP)
projects.description: Given N cities, flight costs, source `src`, destination `dst`, and integer `K`, find cheapest flight cost from `src` to `dst` with AT MOST K STOPS (at most `K+1` edges). Execute Bellman-Ford algorithm for EXACTLY `K+1` relaxation passes in O(K * E) time! In this project, you will build Cheapest Flights K Stops Solver in C.
projects.learningOutcome: K-Stop Bounded Shortest Paths, Multi-Pass Bellman-Ford DP & Distance Array Snapshots
projects.exampleText: Find cheapest flight cost within K=1 stops
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Cheapest Flights Within K Stops (Bellman-Ford / BFS DP) ---
Cheapest flight cost from src to dst within K=1 stops = 200
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Distance Copy**: Copy `prev_dist` array at start of each pass to enforce at most 1 additional step per round.
2. **K+1 Passes**: Run edge relaxations for exactly `K+1` iterations.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `cheapest_flights_k_stops_demo()`: Solves Cheapest Flights Within K Stops via Bellman-Ford DP.

projects.title: Path with Maximum Probability (Logarithmic Weight Dijkstra)
projects.description: Given undirected graph where edge weights represent success probabilities `0 <= prob <= 1`, find path from source to target with MAXIMUM success probability. Maximize product `prob1 * prob2 * ...` by taking negative logarithm `-log(prob)` and using Min-Heap Dijkstra in O(E log V) time! In this project, you will build Max Probability Path Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Probability Multiplication to Log Sum Conversion, Max-Heap Dijkstra & Probability Paths
projects.exampleText: Find path with maximum success probability
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Path with Maximum Probability (Logarithmic Weight Dijkstra) ---
Maximum Success Probability = 0.25000
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Max-Heap Priority**: Store max probability in Priority Queue.
2. **Relaxation**: `if (prob[u] * edge_prob > prob[v]) prob[v] = prob[u] * edge_prob`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `max_probability_path_demo()`: Solves Path with Maximum Probability using Max-Heap Dijkstra.

projects.title: Path with Minimum Effort (Grid Dijkstra Min-Max Height Difference)
projects.description: Given an `R x C` height matrix, find path from top-left `(0,0)` to bottom-right `(R-1, C-1)` that MINIMIZES the maximum absolute height difference between adjacent cells along the path. Use Min-Heap Dijkstra over 2D grid in O(R * C log(R * C)) time! In this project, you will build Path with Minimum Effort Solver in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Grid Min-Max Path Optimization, 2D Grid Dijkstra & Height Effort Minimization
projects.exampleText: Compute minimum effort path on 2D height grid
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Path with Minimum Effort (Grid Dijkstra Min-Max Height Diff) ---
Minimum Effort Path Cost = 2
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Effort Metric**: `effort[v] = max(effort[u], abs(height[u] - height[v]))`.
2. **Grid Dijkstra**: Min-Heap pops minimum effort cell next.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `min_effort_path_demo()`: Solves Path with Minimum Effort using Grid Dijkstra.

projects.title: Swim in Rising Water (Binary Search + BFS / Priority Queue)
projects.description: Given an `N x N` elevation grid, water level at time T allows swimming to cells with elevation `<= T`. Find minimum time T to reach bottom-right `(N-1, N-1)`. Solve using Priority Queue Dijkstra (or Binary Search on T + BFS) in O(N^2 log N) time! In this project, you will build Swim in Rising Water Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Time Threshold Bottlenecks, Priority Queue Grid Search & Water Elevation Min-Max
projects.exampleText: Find minimum time to swim to destination grid cell
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Swim in Rising Water (Min-Max Priority Queue Dijkstra) ---
Minimum Time to reach destination = 16
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Time Metric**: `time[v] = max(time[u], grid[v])`.
2. **Priority Queue**: Min-Heap extracts cell with lowest time threshold.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `swim_in_rising_water_demo()`: Solves Swim in Rising Water using Priority Queue.

projects.title: Shortest Path with Alternating Colors (State-Space BFS)
projects.description: Given directed graph with red and blue edges, find shortest path from source 0 to all nodes such that edge colors ALTERNATE between red and blue along path. State tuple `(node, edge_color)` doubles BFS queue states to `2 * V` in O(V + E) time! In this project, you will build Alternating Colors BFS Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: State-Space Expansion `(node, color)`, Color Constraint Transitions & BFS Shortest Paths
projects.exampleText: Find shortest alternating color path lengths to all nodes
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Shortest Path with Alternating Colors (State-Space BFS) ---
Shortest Alternating Color Distances: [ 0: 0, 1: 1, 2: 2, 3: 3 ]
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **State Tuple**: BFS queue stores `(u, color)` where color is RED or BLUE.
2. **Alternating Transition**: Expand RED edges if previous step was BLUE, and vice versa.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `alternating_colors_shortest_path_demo()`: Solves shortest path with alternating edge colors using state-space BFS.

projects.title: Critical Connections in a Network (Tarjan's Bridge Finder)
projects.description: Find all critical connections (bridges) in a server network of N servers. A connection is critical if removing it disconnects the network. Execute Tarjan's Low-Link DFS algorithm in single O(V + E) pass! In this project, you will build Critical Connections Network Analyzer in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Network Infrastructure Reliability, Tarjan's Bridge Detection & Low-Link DFS Analysis
projects.exampleText: Find critical network connection edges
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Critical Connections in a Network (Tarjan's Bridge Finder) ---
Critical Network Connections (Bridges): [ (1, 3) ]
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Discovery & Low Time**: Track `tin[u]` and `low[u]` during DFS traversal.
2. **Critical Edge**: Edge `(u, v)` is critical bridge if `low[v] > tin[u]`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `critical_connections_demo()`: Solves Critical Connections in a Network using Tarjan's bridge finder.

projects.title: Shortest Path Visiting All Nodes (Graph State BFS)
projects.description: Find shortest path length visiting all N nodes in undirected graph. Represent state as `(curr_node, visited_bitmask)`. Graph state space contains `N * 2^N` states. Multi-source BFS guarantees shortest path in O(N * 2^N) time! In this project, you will build Shortest Path All Nodes Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Bitmask Graph BFS States, Multi-Source Initializations & Visited Node Sets
projects.exampleText: Find shortest path visiting all 4 graph nodes
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Shortest Path Visiting All Nodes (Bitmask BFS) ---
Minimum edges to visit all nodes = 4
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **State Space**: Queue holds tuple `(node, bitmask)`.
2. **BFS Expansion**: Transition to `(neighbor, bitmask | (1 << neighbor))`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `shortest_path_visiting_all_demo()`: Solves shortest path visiting all nodes via bitmask BFS.

projects.title: Minimum Cost to Reach Destination in Time (State DP + Dijkstra)
projects.description: Given graph where edges have travel times and nodes have passage fees, find minimum fee to travel from source to destination within `maxTime`. Combine Dijkstra's algorithm with 2D State DP `dist[node][time]` in O(E * maxTime) time! In this project, you will build Destination Min Fee Solver in C.
projects.learningOutcome: 2D State DP Dijkstra `dist[node][time]`, Time Limit Constraints & Fee Minimization

Minimum Cost within Max Time = 48
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **2D State Array**: `dist[node][time]` tracks minimum fee at specific accumulated travel time.
2. **State Pruning**: Prune path if accumulated time exceeds `maxTime`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `min_cost_destination_time_demo()`: Solves Minimum Cost to Reach Destination in Time.

projects.title: Johnson's Algorithm for Sparse All-Pairs Shortest Paths
projects.description: Johnson's algorithm computes All-Pairs Shortest Paths on sparse graphs with negative edge weights in `O(V^2 log V + V * E)` time (faster than Floyd-Warshall `O(V^3)`). Uses Bellman-Ford to compute potential vertex weights `h[u]`, re-weights all edges to non-negative `w' = w + h[u] - h[v]`, then runs Dijkstra V times! In this project, you will build Johnson's Algorithm Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Johnson's Algorithm, Edge Potential Re-weighting & Sparse Graph All-Pairs Optimizations
projects.exampleText: Compute all-pairs shortest paths on sparse graph with negative edges
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Johnson's Algorithm for Sparse All-Pairs Shortest Paths ---
Re-weighted graph with Bellman-Ford potential, executed V Dijkstra queries in O(V^2 log V + VE) time.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Potential Re-weighting**: Add super-node, run Bellman-Ford to get `h[u]`. Re-weight `w' = w + h[u] - h[v] >= 0`.
2. **V Dijkstra Runs**: Run non-negative Dijkstra starting from each vertex.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `johnson_algorithm_demo()`: Solves sparse all-pairs shortest paths using Johnson's algorithm.

projects.title: SPFA (Shortest Path Faster Algorithm - Queue-based Bellman-Ford)
projects.description: Shortest Path Faster Algorithm (SPFA) is an optimized queue-based version of Bellman-Ford that relaxes ONLY vertices whose distances were updated in previous step. Runs in `O(E)` average time on random graphs! In this project, you will build SPFA Shortest Path Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: SPFA Algorithm, Queue-based Edge Relaxations & Average-Case O(E) Speedup
projects.exampleText: Execute queue-based SPFA shortest path algorithm
projects.exampleOutput:
--- SPFA (Shortest Path Faster Algorithm) ---
Executed Queue-based Bellman-Ford (SPFA) in O(E) average time.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **In-Queue Flag**: Maintain `in_queue[u]` array to prevent duplicate queue pushes.
2. **Selective Relaxation**: Pop node `u` from queue; relax neighbors `v` and push `v` to queue if updated and not in queue.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `spfa_algorithm_demo()`: Solves single-source shortest paths using SPFA algorithm.

projects.title: A* Search Algorithm with Manhattan & Euclidean Heuristic Engine
projects.description: The A* Search Algorithm evaluates nodes using evaluation function `f(n) = g(n) + h(n)`, where `g(n)` is exact distance from start and `h(n)` is an admissible heuristic estimate to target (Manhattan or Euclidean distance). Prunes search space by 90%! In this project, you will build A* Search Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: A* Search Algorithm, Admissible Heuristic Functions (`f = g + h`) & Search Space Pruning
projects.exampleText: Evaluate A* search pathfinding with Manhattan heuristic
projects.exampleOutput:
--- A* Search Algorithm with Manhattan & Euclidean Heuristic Engine ---
Executed A* search using f(n) = g(n) + h(n). Found optimal path in 15 node evaluations.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Evaluation Function**: `f_score = g_score + heuristic(node, target)`.
2. **Min-Heap Priority**: Priority Queue extracts node with lowest `f_score` next.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `a_star_search_demo()`: Implements A* search algorithm with heuristic functions.

projects.title: Contraction Hierarchies (CH) Highway Acceleration Engine
projects.description: Contraction Hierarchies (CH) preprocesses continental road networks (e.g. 50,000,000 nodes) by contracting minor nodes and adding shortcut edges. Reduces shortest path query time from 2 seconds down to 0.05 milliseconds (40,000x speedup)! In this project, you will build Contraction Hierarchies Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Contraction Hierarchies (CH), Node Contraction & Microsecond Highway Navigation
projects.exampleText: Preprocess road network and answer CH query in 0.05ms
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Contraction Hierarchies (CH) Highway Acceleration Engine ---
Preprocessed continental road network into node shortcuts. Distance Query Answered in 0.05ms!
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Node Contraction**: Order nodes by importance; contract node `x` by adding shortcut edges between neighbors.
2. **Bidirectional Search**: Query runs forward and backward searches only on upward importance edges.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `contraction_hierarchies_demo()`: Solves Contraction Hierarchies highway route acceleration.

projects.title: Suurballe's Algorithm for Disjoint Edge-Path Pairs
projects.description: Suurballe's algorithm finds TWO edge-disjoint paths between source and destination in a weighted directed graph such that total combined weight of both paths is MINIMIZED. Uses Dijkstra, edge reversal, and potential re-weighting in `O(E log V)` time! In this project, you will build Suurballe's Algorithm Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Suurballe's Algorithm, Edge-Disjoint Path Minimization & Dual Network Paths
projects.exampleText: Find 2 edge-disjoint shortest path pairs
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Suurballe's Algorithm for Disjoint Edge-Path Pairs ---
Found 2 edge-disjoint shortest paths with minimum total distance = 42
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **First Dijkstra Path**: Find 1st shortest path P1; transform edge weights using `dist` potential.
2. **Edge Inversion**: Reverse P1 edges and run 2nd Dijkstra; combine paths to yield 2 disjoint paths.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `suurballe_algorithm_demo()`: Solves Suurballe's algorithm for edge-disjoint path pairs.
